statement: The function returns a result res (it does not fail) and res equals the number of pairs (l, r) with 0 <= l <= r < len(nums) such that the bitwise XOR of nums[l], nums[l+1], ..., nums[r] is 0. Equivalently, for every bit position k >= 0, the number of indices t in [l, r] whose kth binary bit is 1 is even.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: For every nums satisfying the preconditions, beautiful_subarrays nums returns a result (Result.ok res for some integer res); it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access out of bounds.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever beautiful_subarrays nums returns a result res, 0 <= res <= len(nums)*(len(nums)+1)/2.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever beautiful_subarrays nums returns a result res, res >= the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i] = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever beautiful_subarrays nums returns a result res, res >= the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(nums) - 1 and nums[i] = nums[i+1].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let nums_rev be the array of length len(nums) defined by nums_rev[i] = nums[len(nums)-1-i] for 0 <= i < len(nums). For every nums satisfying the preconditions, if beautiful_subarrays nums returns res and beautiful_subarrays nums_rev returns res_rev, then res = res_rev.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Let P be defined by P[0] = 0 and, for 1 <= t <= len(nums), P[t] = the bitwise XOR of nums[0], nums[1], ..., nums[t-1]. Whenever beautiful_subarrays nums returns a result res, res equals the number of pairs (a, b) with 0 <= a < b <= len(nums) and P[a] = P[b].
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever beautiful_subarrays nums returns a result res, res = 0 if and only if all len(nums)+1 prefix XORs P[0], P[1], ..., P[len(nums)] are pairwise distinct, where P[0] = 0 and P[t] = nums[0] xor ... xor nums[t-1] for 1 <= t <= len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever beautiful_subarrays nums returns a result res, res = len(nums)*(len(nums)+1)/2 if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000.

statement: Whenever beautiful_subarrays nums returns a result res, res <= len(nums)*(len(nums)+1)/2 - len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) >= 1 and len(nums) <= 100000, and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= nums[i] <= 1000000. Additionally for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] != 0.
